finding.claim: Unvalidated callbackUrl stored by subscribe() is used by notifyAll() as the target of an outbound HTTP POST, enabling blind SSRF to internal hosts or ports the attacker chooses.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe(name, callbackUrl) at src/Jobs.java:13, which per the comment at line 12 comes from the body of POST /subscribe. Anyone who can reach that endpoint controls it. The handler is not in this repository.
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) at src/Jobs.java:24, where req is a POST built from URI.create(cb) at line 21.

trace.note: subscribe() stores callbackUrl into the subscriptions map with no validation.
subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) keeps the raw attacker-supplied string.
Comment says notifyAll runs every minute. The scheduler is not in this repository.
notifyAll iterates over every subscriptions value.
URI.create(cb) performs a syntax check only, with no host, IP, port, or scheme allow-list.
POST request built with the payload as body and the attacker URL as target.
client.send issues the request. The response body is read but discarded, so the attacker gets no response data (blind).

finding.guards_checked: subscribe() (lines 13-15) performs no validation. notifyAll() (lines 18-26) performs no host, IP, port, or redirect checks. The only restriction is that HttpRequest.Builder.uri() rejects non-http(s) schemes, which does not block localhost, RFC1918 addresses, or 169.254.169.254. The client at line 10 is HttpClient.newHttpClient(), whose default redirect policy is NEVER, so no redirect hop is added. The handler for POST /subscribe was not available to check for validation upstream.

verdict.guard_found: none in src/Jobs.java: subscribe() at lines 13-15 stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and notifyAll() at lines 19-24 applies no host, IP, port, or scheme check before client.send. The only file in the repo is src/Jobs.java, so no upstream handler guard is visible.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (src/Jobs.java:14 stores the raw string, :21 passes it to URI.create, :24 sends it), and no guard exists in this file, but the attacker-control premise rests on the handler for POST /subscribe (the comment at line 12 is the only evidence), which is not in the repo, so whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege caller can set callbackUrl cannot be decided from the code available.
